changes_made.explanation: This paper is about conversational search retrieval, not NLG. It evaluates retrieval systems (dense retrievers) that find relevant passages, not text generation. While CQR (Conversational Query Rewriting) is mentioned as a baseline approach, the paper does not evaluate or study NLG tasks - it focuses on retrieval evaluation using metrics like MRR and Recall.
The paper uses retrieval evaluation metrics (MRR, Recall@K) to evaluate retrieval performance, not NLG evaluation metrics. These are not metrics for evaluating generated text quality.
No LLMs are used as judges for evaluating generated outputs in this paper.
No human evaluation of generated outputs is conducted in this paper.

overall_notes: This paper is fundamentally about retrieval evaluation in conversational search, not NLG evaluation. The core contribution is analyzing 'shortcut dependency' in dense retrievers and proposing hard negative mining strategies to improve retrieval robustness. While CQR (Conversational Query Rewriting) is mentioned as an alternative approach, the paper does not evaluate or study NLG systems - it focuses entirely on retrieval system evaluation using standard IR metrics.
